rural_facts: The Future of Rural England Report was published on 16 July 2026.
Gigabit-capable broadband was available to 66% of premises in rural residential areas, compared with 93% in urban areas.
Approximately 21,218 rural premises in England, representing 0.6% of rural premises, lacked decent fixed-line or fixed-wireless broadband.
The report stated that 4,000 residential premises were eligible for the broadband Universal Service Obligation as of January 2026.
Indoor 4G coverage from all four reported mobile operators reached 63% of rural premises, compared with 96% of urban premises.
Approximately 2% of rural areas had no indoor 4G coverage from any mobile network operator.
Standalone 5G was available outside 81% of rural premises in England in January 2026, compared with 97% of urban premises.
The government goal stated in the report is at least 99% UK gigabit-capable premises coverage by 2032.
By the end of December 2025, government-funded programmes had upgraded more than 1.3 million rural and hard-to-reach premises to gigabit-capable broadband.
The Shared Rural Network had met its core objective of 95% geographic 4G coverage from at least one mobile operator one year ahead of schedule.
The report recorded 35 upgraded Shared Rural Network masts delivering new coverage in rural England.
Targeted Shared Rural Network delivery was scheduled to continue through January 2027.
The Connectivity and Accessibility Statistics for Rural England page was updated on 22 July 2026 with July 2026 broadband and mobile-coverage analysis.
The Ofcom-commissioned rail study covered 50 journeys on 24 rail lines in February and March 2026.
